transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-12-09
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions), Marco Ruiz (CTO - Veridian), Janelle Brooks (ML Lead), Kenji Watanabe (SRE), Priya Solanki (Product)
Links shared: Veridian sample dataset (internal link), benchmarking sheet (https://tiny.link/veridian-bench), Redwood security packet (link)

[00:00] Lena Park: all right everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, so we'll try to cover scope, success criteria, model shortlist and the bench plan. quick around the room? Marco, do you want to kick off with the core ask?

[00:18] Marco Ruiz: yeah thanks Lena. The tl;dr is — we want to surface root-cause hints from device telemetry and short log snippets. Most inputs are one-off log messages or stacks, sometimes short sequences up to say 400 tokens. Key metrics: accuracy of root-cause classification, ability to extract structured fields, and latency for interactive troubleshooting flows. The business deadline is Q1 pilot, so we need a 2-4 week POC to pick model + infra.

[00:45] Janelle Brooks: to add, we also want multilingual support for EU / APAC customers — not huge volume but non-trivial: Spanish, Japanese logs mainly. so multilingual competence is on the rubric.

[01:05] Omar Singh: great. couple of clarifying stats from my side — can you share target throughput and token sizes? you mentioned 400 tokens max, what about concurrency?

[01:15] Kenji Watanabe: peak concurrent users is around 400 at certain support peaks, steady state 30-60. avg tokens per request ~120, but the extraction workflows can ask follow-ups and hit context windows up to 2k in some cases. We can anonymize the dataset; i'll upload traces.

[01:34] Lena Park: perfect. So for the POC we should size for peak-ish behavior but run bench tiers: baseline (50 rps), peak (400 concurrent sessions). We'll propose both hosted and dedicated runs so you can compare cost vs tail latency.

[01:50] Marco Ruiz: yes exactly. Also security constraints: data is sensitive. We need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration and audit logs. We also may want a VPC/private control plane for the pilot if the numbers look right.

[02:10] Lena Park: understood — we have SOC2 docs and we can map the KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include the security packet. For a POC with private, there's some extra setup time — typically a week to provision a private VPC deployment, longer if air-gapped.

[02:30] Ravi Patel: quick note on quality tradeoffs: since telemetry language is terse, hallucination rates are sensitive — smaller models sometimes invent plausible but wrong root causes. We should evaluate F1 for structured extraction, and a separate hallucination rate metric.

[02:48] Janelle Brooks: yes, and we care about confidence calibration — when model says it's unsure we want to route to human. so thresholding and confidence props matter.

[03:05] Omar Singh: cool. Let's walk model shortlist. Based on your workload (short to medium context, multilingual, extraction heavy), our candidate open models are: Llama-2-13B-Open, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Mistral-Inst-13B (we saw better structured output), Falcon-40B-Instruct (if you need larger capacity), and Mosaic MPT-30B for long sequences. There's also a couple of newer quantized variants (e.g., Llama-2-13B-4bit, Mistral-13B-8bit) — but quantization can impact extraction fidelity.

[03:40] Marco Ruiz: any Redwood-verified variants or tuned checkpoints that do better on structured extraction?

[03:48] Omar Singh: we have some Redwood-verified profiles and tuned decoding configs — we'll include those in the shortlist. One note: Falcon and MPT are heavy; they give better recall for some tasks but at cost of higher latency and infra spend. Mistral-13B often hits a good cost/accuracy sweet spot for short-to-medium context tasks.

[04:12] Priya Solanki: what about multilingual — do these models handle Japanese idioms in logs?

[04:20] Janelle Brooks: we ran a small internal eval where Mistral variants handled Spanish fine but Japanese degraded; Llama-2-13B with additional fine-tune did better for Japanese. So language-specific micro-fine-tuning may be needed.

[04:40] Omar Singh: exactly. For POC we'll include a language axis in the bench: English, Spanish, Japanese. We can run multilingual prompts and measure extraction accuracy per language. For Japanese we might recommend a small adapter or light fine-tune as a post-POC step.

[05:00] Lena Park: switching to bench metrics — what do we want to capture? Proposal: latency p50/p95/p99 for both token streaming and final response, throughput, extraction F1, hallucination rate, memory / GPU utilization, and KV cache hit-rate for repeated prefixes (since many logs share device metadata). Anything else?

[05:25] Marco Ruiz: add tokenization inefficiencies — logs have weird tokens (paths, hex dumps) that blow up token counts. so tokenization overhead per request is an important cost factor.

[05:40] Omar Singh: good point. We'll add tokenization overhead and a cost-per-1M-tokens projection for each model in hosted and dedicated setups. We'll test quantized configs too: 4-bit, int8, and fp16 where supported. Note: 4-bit saves cost but sometimes drops extraction recall.

[06:05] Kenji Watanabe: what's the expected duration of the POC run? you mentioned 2 weeks earlier?

[06:12] Lena Park: typical POC is 2 weeks of benchmark + 1 week to analyze and present results — so 3 weeks total. If you want private deployment initial setup, tack on ~1 additional week. So plan: bench window week of Dec 20 (2 weeks), results by Jan 10. That hits your Q1 pilot runway.

[06:32] Marco Ruiz: timeline works if we get the benchmark harness ready and we upload data this week. Kenji will take the upload action.

[06:40] Janelle Brooks: on evaluation rubric — can we use a weighted score? e.g., 40% extraction F1, 25% latency (p95), 20% cost, 15% multilingual recall.

[06:55] Ravi Patel: yes that sounds reasonable. We'll include that weighting in the results dashboard.

[07:05] Speaker 1 (background): [inaudible]...

[07:12] Omar Singh: i want to call out a couple of implementation notes: 1) context window support — if you hit 2k contexts, some smaller models degrade rapidly; 2) KV cache behavior — Redwood runtime tries to reuse KV across similar prefixes to reduce token compute; we'll measure cache hit rates; 3) routing policies — if you have a hybrid setup, we can route critical low-latency flows to smaller pinned models and heavy recall tasks to larger models.

[07:45] Marco Ruiz: nice, can you do a cost comparison showing a hybrid routing policy?

[07:52] Lena Park: yes we'll include a hybrid scenario in the cost appendix.

[08:00] Priya Solanki: there's also a procedural constraint: legal wants to see how long data is retained. We need TTLs, audit logs, and KMS key lifecycle info.

[08:10] Lena Park: noted. we'll attach retention and KMS info and sample audit logs.

[08:18] Kenji Watanabe: regarding the benchmark environment — can we test both on hosted Redwood infra and a Dedicated reserved GPU? I want to see real tail latency differences.

[08:28] Omar Singh: yes, plan is to run each model in two modes: Redwood hosted (fast onboarding) and Dedicated pool with pinned GPUs. For private VPC we can also run, but that requires provisioning. We'll quantify the delta.

[08:44] Janelle Brooks: what GPUs do you recommend for Dedicated? A100s or H100s?

[08:50] Omar Singh: for FP16 / int8, A100 is fine. For large-context or memory-heavy models H100 helps, but it's more expensive. We'll include recommended GPU types per model in the shortlist.

[09:05] Marco Ruiz: hold on, what's the expected cost delta for Falcon-40B vs Mistral-13B? ballpark numbers?

[09:12] Omar Singh: rough ballpark: Falcon-40B could be 2.5–3x cost per token compared to Mistral-13B in fp16 on similar infra, and latency can be 1.5–2x at p95. We'll put concrete numbers in the model table.

[09:28] Lena Park: ok i'll capture that and send a modeled cost table.

[09:35] Marco Ruiz: any concerns about hallucinations on structured fields? we need conservative answers.

[09:40] Omar Singh: smaller models tend to hallucinate more for unfamiliar technical terms — for telemetry that means invented causes. We recommend a few mitigations: 1) prompt engineering with strict output schema, 2) light fine-tuning or chain-of-thought-free decoding, 3) confidence calibration and human fallback. We'll test these in the POC.

[10:00] Janelle Brooks: can Redwood run the fine-tune / adapter step during the POC or is that post-POC?

[10:07] Omar Singh: we can include a small adapter experiment in the POC (week 2) if you agree. The adapter can be trained on ~500–1k labeled examples and often gives big gains on domain-specific extraction. There is extra compute but it's doable.

[10:25] Marco Ruiz: sounds good — let's add that as an optional track.

[10:30] Priya Solanki: about logs — we will remove PII, but some device IDs remain; we need to make sure KMS encrypts data at rest and in transit.

[10:38] Lena Park: confirmed. we'll provide the encryption matrix.

[10:45] Ravi Patel: one more technical deep-dive item: tokenization. we should run the same tokenizer across all models to make apples-to-apples comparisons, but note tokenizers differ in token counts — that will affect cost. We'll include normalized cost metrics as well as raw tokens.

[11:05] Kenji Watanabe: for the bench harness can you also collect memory fragmentation and cold-start times? we see cold starts impact p99 when autoscaling.

[11:12] Omar Singh: yes we'll capture cold-starts and autoscale behavior; we'll also try burst tests to simulate support spikes.

[11:25] Lena Park: summary and next steps: 1) Redwood sends model shortlist + tuned configs by Dec 13, 2) Veridian uploads anonymized sample logs to the benchmarking sheet by Dec 12 (Kenji), 3) Redwood prepares harness and bench runbook by Dec 16, 4) schedule bench window week of Dec 20 for two-weeks.

[11:45] Marco Ruiz: agreed. One ask — can you include a recommended canary rollout plan if we choose Dedicated after the POC? we may want A/B with traffic split.

[11:55] Lena Park: yes we'll include rollout steps and fallback policies.

[12:00] Janelle Brooks: thanks everyone, this was productive.

[12:05] Lena Park: thanks, meeting end. We'll follow up via email with the model shortlist and the security packet.

Action items recap (verbatim):

End of transcript.
